claims.text: As-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 has a predominantly FCC microstructure.
The as-built alloy contains residual stresses, microsegregation, and non-equilibrium features characteristic of additive manufacturing.
Degradation of the target alloy in oxidizing gas is governed by element-selective surface oxidation.
Surface reduction governs degradation of the target alloy in reducing gas.
Surface oxidation or reduction depletes Al and/or Cr at grain boundaries in the target alloy.
Al or Cr depletion promotes formation of discontinuous or non-protective oxide scales.
Non-protective scales cannot accommodate thermal stresses and consequently cause interfacial cracking and catastrophic failure.
A thin Cr-enriching deposit or Al-retaining surface treatment can be applied while leaving the bulk microstructure unaltered.
Oxide-scale structure and elemental distributions at grain boundaries mediate the exposed alloy's response.
A continuous, adherent oxide scale protects the alloy better than a discontinuous or spalled scale.
Discontinuous or spalled oxide scales promote crack initiation.
Changing the surface concentration of reactive elements changes the local chemical potential at the alloy surface.
Reactive-element surface enrichment promotes a coherent protective oxide and retards further elemental depletion in oxidizing environments.
The untreated target alloy oxidizes unevenly, producing local stresses, scale spallation, and microcracks along weakened grain boundaries.
Surface-enriched specimens will form more continuous and adherent oxide scales than untreated specimens.
Surface-enriched specimens will have lower oxide growth rates and delayed microcrack initiation relative to the untreated baseline.
Differences in oxidation and reduction kinetics in reducing atmospheres will alter oxide-scale characteristics and damage initiation.
The proposed mechanism applies from 700 to 1100 degrees Celsius in both oxygen-rich and hydrogen-containing atmospheres.
Failure of surface enrichment to improve scale continuity or adhesion and to delay microcracking or catastrophic failure would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
